title: US general election — president, the full House, one third of the Senate; the corridor this calendar's furthest-out entry actually sits inside
source: EST: the date is statutory and was computed, not fetched -- 2 U.S.C. section 7 fixes the federal election on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November of an even year, and for 2028 the first Monday is November 6, so Election Day is Tuesday 2028-11-07 (weekday arithmetic, reproducible). Independently cross-checked by an identity rather than a source: this calendar's fed-board-closure-2028-11-10 exists because Veterans Day 2028-11-11 falls on a Saturday, and Nov 11 lands on a Saturday exactly when Nov 7 is the Tuesday after the first Monday -- so every one of the seven prior instances (1978, 1989, 1995, 2000, 2006, 2017, 2023) has Election Day on Nov 7 and the Board-closure Friday at D+3, verified by computation over all seven. No primary source was fetched and this calendar has no source prefix for a statute, which is why this is EST: and not confirmed -- the same honest reading the sibling midterm-elections-2026-11-03 entry records: date-certain, outcome-unknown. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED by the fed-board-closure-2028-11-10 initial research (2026-09-09), whose own corridor sweep -- run mechanically against all 765 tracked events and proposals -- returned NOTHING but itself at plus or minus 5 days AND at plus or minus 60 days. That is the finding behind this proposal: 2028-11-10 is currently this calendar's furthest-out entry (the next-latest is 2028-02-16), and the single event that actually dominates its session is not on the calendar at all. The proposer measured the dominance rather than assuming it. Fridays at D+3 of a PRESIDENTIAL election week, 1976-2024: n=13, mean -0.202%, mean absolute move 0.889% against a 0.717% all-Fridays base (permutation P = 0.180, NOT significant), but 4 of 13 moved at least 1.5% against an 11.82% base rate (binomial P = 0.058, which fails multiple-comparison discipline and is reported as suggestive, never as an edge). The full election week itself is where the dispersion actually lives: n=13, mean absolute week move 2.793%, range -4.62% (2000) to +6.02% (2020). NOTHING TRADEABLE IS CLAIMED HERE and no direction is implied -- the receiving lane should note that the sibling midterm-elections-2026-11-03 ledger already rejects the generic post-election-rally statistic as uncontrolled for unconditional drift, and should not re-import it. Impact is filed high to match that sibling's tier, inherited rather than measured. symbols is empty. Proposed as an estimate; estimate widens caution and licenses no entry.
